answer: Seed each grading round with canary answers: deliberately broken submissions whose correct verdict is fixed in advance, hidden among the real ones. A sybil juror-ring that rubber-stamps its own clones to farm rewards waves these canaries through too, lighting its trail like a comet across a dark panel. Every grader is a vertex in the trust graph; approve a canary and that vertex is flagged, so the next slashing tide sweeps its bonded stake. Cost to attacker: one approved canary burns the whole colluding ring's bonds, so faking N jurors risks N times the bond per panel. Collusion stops paying.
